transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. My name is Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hey, Dr. Smith. Yeah, um, I guess what brought me in is... well, I went from just being a normal crew guy on my landscaping team to suddenly trying to run, like, three different bids at once. Which, man, dealing with the city is a total joke. My buddy Dave works for the water department down there, and he was telling me they haven't updated the mainline pipes since the 80s. We actually dug up this rusted piece of junk on a job Tuesday that looked like it belonged on the Titanic. 

But, uh, anyway, I was calling all these city people and trying to line up wholesale plant suppliers. I got super into hydrangeas for a second—did you know the soil pH completely changes their color? Like, if you dump coffee grounds in the dirt, it changes everything. But yeah, I was messaging literally everybody I knew about this massive community park idea I had, and it was just... I don't know, it was like I couldn't shut it off. Just going and going. I should probably text Dave back about that truck he's selling, actually. Wait, what did you ask me?
How long has this burst of energy and racing activity been going on—days, weeks?

Man, it was... I'd say it was about two weeks. That whole fired-up, overconfident stretch really started when I decided I needed to completely remake myself for that park pitch. I actually went out and bought all these new clothes because I figured, you know, you gotta look the part if you're dealing with city money. 

I went to this massive thrift store off Route 9—have you been there? The one next to the old diner? They have the craziest stuff. I found this vintage leather jacket that was in perfect condition. The guy working the register, Gary I think his name was, he was telling me it belonged to some local musician back in the 90s. Gary's a total trip, he was talking my ear off about the local grunge scene and how all the venues shut down. 

But yeah, I was wearing that jacket everywhere, just feeling absolutely untouchable for those two weeks. And then... man, I just crashed. Like, hit a total brick wall. I don't even know where that jacket is right now. Probably in the back of my truck. My truck needs an oil change so bad, actually, the check engine light has been on since Thursday... wait, what were we talking about? Days or weeks, right. Yeah, two weeks.
During those two weeks of high energy, were you using any stimulants, like cocaine, amphetamines, or diet pills, or drinking a lot more caffeine or energy drinks than usual?

No, man, nothing like that. No cocaine or speed or anything. I mean, I drink coffee, but just my regular amount. I usually grab a large from that gas station on the corner of Elm and 4th before I head to the site. You know the one? The guy who runs it, Sam, he makes the best breakfast sandwiches. He gets the sausage from this local farm out past the county line. I was actually thinking about driving out there this weekend to see if they sell direct, because grocery store meat is just getting ridiculously expensive. I mean, a pound of ground beef is like eight bucks now. It's crazy. I was talking to my mom about it, and she was saying how back in her day... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, stimulants. No, just my regular morning coffee.

During those two weeks of feeling 'untouchable' and full of energy, did you have any experiences like hearing voices others couldn't hear, or holding beliefs—like having special powers or a special mission—that others told you weren't true?

No, no voices or anything like that. I didn't think I had superpowers or whatever. I just felt really, really good about my ideas, you know? Like that park pitch. I mean, I really thought it was a solid plan. The city council should honestly be looking at unused lots like the one behind the old bowling alley. That place has been sitting empty since, what, 2018? I used to go bowling there all the time in high school. They had this arcade game, Time Crisis, and me and my buddy Mark would spend hours on it. Mark actually moved to Florida last year, somewhere near Tampa, I think. He says the humidity is brutal but the fishing is great. I've always wanted to try deep-sea fishing. You ever been? Catching a marlin or something would be insane. But yeah, no, I wasn't hearing voices or thinking I was a superhero or anything. Just felt super dialed in.

Before these last two weeks, have you ever had a period—lasting a week or more—where you felt unusually low, hopeless, or lost interest in things, or another time where you felt this same kind of high energy?

Yeah, I mean... the low part, feeling hopeless, that's been hanging over me for about a year now. Honestly, this latest crash after the two weeks of feeling good? It's the worst it's ever gotten. I can barely drag myself out of bed to go to work. Which sucks because we just got this huge contract for a new subdivision out past the highway. They're building these massive houses, like, three-car garages, huge backyards. The kind of places that need a full crew just to keep the grass cut. 

My boss, Rick, he's been stressing out about getting enough guys for the job. He actually asked me if I knew anyone looking for work. I told him maybe my cousin, but my cousin is always flaking out on things. He got a job at a warehouse last month and quit after two days because they wouldn't let him listen to music on the floor. Can you believe that? I mean, I get safety rules, but come on, it's just music. I always have my headphones in when I'm on the mower. It's the only way to get through the day, just zoning out to some classic rock. Led Zeppelin, Pink Floyd... you know, the good stuff. They just don't make music like that anymore. Everything on the radio now just sounds like computers... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the low periods. Yeah, it's been about a year of feeling really down, and this crash is just brutal. But before that, I don't really remember having another time where I felt that super high energy, just this last time.
During this past year of feeling down, especially now during the crash, have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that you'd be better off dead?

Yeah... yeah, it's gotten really dark lately. Honestly, I got really scared the other day. I was just sitting in my truck after work, you know, the F-150 I bought a couple years ago. I love that truck, it's got the extended cab and everything. I actually had to replace the alternator on it last month, which was a total pain because the parts store gave me the wrong one first. I had it all torn apart in the driveway, grease everywhere, and then I realized the mounting bracket didn't line up. So I had to put it all back together, drive back to the store, and argue with the kid behind the counter. He looked like he was barely out of high school, probably didn't even know how to change a tire, let alone cross-reference a part number. I swear, customer service is just dead these days. You go anywhere and people are just staring at their phones... 

But anyway, I was sitting in the truck after work, and... it wasn't just that feeling of wanting to disappear or go to sleep and not wake up anymore. I was actually sitting there looking around the cab, looking at the tools and stuff I had in there, and thinking about exactly how I could just... end it. Right then and there, with what I had. It really freaked me out.
